summary: A vendor approved in Plinth becomes a NetSuite vendor record, and a signed contract raises its purchase order. Bills and payment status come back, so the contract shows what has been paid.
syncs: Vendors, purchase orders, bills and payment status, every 15 minutes
setup: About an hour with a NetSuite admin, through a SuiteTalk integration role

summary: Vendors and bills sync between Plinth and QuickBooks, so a contract shows what has been billed against it without anyone retyping amounts.
syncs: Vendors, bills and payment status, hourly
setup: About 20 minutes; a QuickBooks admin signs in once

summary: Approved vendors and purchase orders flow from Plinth into Intacct, and posted bills flow back to the contract they belong to.
syncs: Vendors, purchase orders, bills and dimensions, every 30 minutes
setup: About an hour with an Intacct admin and a Web Services user

summary: Vendors and purchase orders approved in Plinth are created in Xero. Xero stays the book of record.
syncs: Vendors and purchase orders, Plinth to Xero, hourly
setup: About 15 minutes; a Xero admin signs in once

summary: Plinth reads cost centers, departments and manager relationships from Workday, so approval chains follow your org chart and every contract lands on the right cost center.
syncs: Workers, cost centers and supervisory orgs, Workday to Plinth, nightly
setup: Half a day with a Workday admin, through an integration system user

summary: Customer contracts start from a closed-won opportunity. Plinth pulls the account, the opportunity owner and the order form, so sales never emails a contract to legal.
syncs: Accounts, closed-won opportunities and attached files, Salesforce to Plinth, every 5 minutes
setup: About 30 minutes with a Salesforce admin; a connected app and one permission set

summary: A deal moved to closed won opens a customer contract in Plinth with the company, the deal owner and the quote attached.
syncs: Companies, closed-won deals and quotes, HubSpot to Plinth, every 5 minutes
setup: About 15 minutes; a HubSpot super admin signs in once

summary: Approvals, renewal reminders and questions on a contract land in Slack. An approver reads the summary and approves or sends it back from the message.
syncs: Approval requests, renewal reminders and comments, both ways, as they happen
setup: About 10 minutes; a workspace admin installs the Plinth app

summary: Approvals and renewal reminders arrive as Teams messages with the contract summary, and approvers act on them without opening Plinth.
syncs: Approval requests and renewal reminders, both ways, as they happen
setup: About 20 minutes; a Teams admin approves the Plinth app

summary: A contract leaves Plinth for signature in DocuSign and comes back signed, filed against the vendor, with the signed PDF and the audit trail.
syncs: Envelopes, signer status and signed PDFs, both ways, as they happen
setup: About 15 minutes with a DocuSign admin

summary: Contracts go out for signature from Plinth through Acrobat Sign and return signed, with the audit report attached.
syncs: Agreements, signer status and signed PDFs, both ways, as they happen
setup: About 15 minutes with an Acrobat Sign account admin

summary: People sign in to Plinth with Okta. SCIM creates and removes accounts as people join and leave, and Okta groups map to Plinth roles.
syncs: Users and groups, Okta to Plinth, as they change
setup: About 30 minutes with an Okta admin, SAML and SCIM

summary: Single sign-on through Entra ID, with SCIM provisioning so leavers lose access the day they leave.
syncs: Users and groups, Entra ID to Plinth, as they change
setup: About 30 minutes with an Entra admin, SAML and SCIM

summary: Sign in with Google, and Plinth files each signed contract's PDF in the Drive folder you choose.
syncs: Sign-in, plus signed PDFs to Drive, as they happen
setup: About 10 minutes; a Workspace admin approves the app

summary: A new vendor review or a security questionnaire opens a Jira issue in the queue you choose, and the contract links to it.
syncs: Issues, Plinth to Jira, as they are raised
setup: About 15 minutes with a Jira admin

summary: Every contract, vendor, spend commitment and renewal date lands in your Snowflake account as tables, refreshed nightly, for your own reporting.
syncs: Contracts, vendors, commitments and renewals, Plinth to Snowflake, nightly
setup: About an hour with a Snowflake admin, through a share

summary: If you are moving off Coupa, Plinth imports your supplier list and open contracts from a Coupa export, with the original IDs kept.
syncs: Suppliers and contracts, one-time import
setup: A working session with our team, usually one afternoon

summary: Plinth imports your Ironclad repository with its metadata, so no contract and no renewal date gets lost in a move.
syncs: Contracts, metadata and signed PDFs, one-time import
setup: A working session with our team, usually one afternoon

summary: Vendor card spend in Ramp shows up against the vendor's contract in Plinth, so you see what is contracted next to what is being spent.
syncs: Vendors and transactions, Ramp to Plinth, daily; vendor records, Plinth to Ramp
setup: About 10 minutes; a Ramp admin signs in once

summary: Brex card and bill spend is matched to the vendor's contract in Plinth, so unmanaged spend stands out.
syncs: Vendors and transactions, Brex to Plinth, daily; vendor records, Plinth to Brex
setup: About 10 minutes; a Brex admin signs in once

summary: A Plinth app on Zapier with triggers for new contracts, approvals and renewals, so you can wire Plinth to tools we do not connect to yet.
syncs: Events out and actions in, as they happen
setup: Minutes, by whoever owns your Zapier account
